summary.tldr: Creates National Rabies Awareness Day on September 28 and requires a federal strategy on rabies prevention, testing, vaccination and treatment.
what_it_does: Designates September 28 each year as National Rabies Awareness Day across Canada.
Requires the Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food to develop a national rabies strategy with provinces, Indigenous governing bodies, northern, remote and rural communities, and other stakeholders.
Directs the strategy to improve access to rabies testing, vaccination, prevention and treatment, with a focus on domesticated dogs and other animals.

Calls for measures on vaccine delivery in northern communities, lay vaccination programs, better surveillance and direct rapid immunohistochemical testing, community-led education, humane animal overpopulation measures, and non-surgical contraception.
Requires a report on the strategy within two years, then a review within two more years, with both reports tabled in Parliament and posted online.
summary.background: The bill names the Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food as the federal minister responsible for the strategy. It also sets deadlines for a strategy report and a later review report.
